editorial:
Imagine being stuck in a small room for nearly a year with someone you hate, trying to get them to tell the truth. That is exactly what you get with this movie. You follow Detective Anderson and a guy named Bradley Bandor in a high-stakes game of cat and mouse. The whole vibe is tense and stripped down, focusing entirely on the battle of wills between two people. It feels like a stage play because there are no flashy locations, just two guys talking and fighting with words to see who will break first.

The acting is what really sells this story, as both leads make you feel their frustration and exhaustion. While the pace is slow at times, the dialogue keeps you interested because you are always guessing who is lying. If you enjoy movies that rely on smart talking rather than big explosions, you will love this. You can grab a 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to see every detail on their faces, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend when you want something that makes you think.
endingExplained: By the end, you realize that the power dynamic has shifted completely. The detective thinks he is in control, but Bradley has been playing a much longer game. The twist reveals that the interrogation was not just about a crime, but about breaking the detective's own mind. In the final moments, the truth comes out in a way that leaves you questioning who the real villain is before the screen cuts to black.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological battles and character studies.
